content: mine also has the z motor on the other connector. i think with prusa firmware, both ZR and ZL connectors output the same signal and then the splitter transmits it to all three Z motors. so it shouldnt matter which connector you use. i will leave mine as it is, since it worked that way too. but honestly im a bit disappointed that all three motors get the same signal through a splitter. i would have expected a separate connection for each Z motor, so that the bed can be levelled to perfectly straight for every print by the Z motors.
My printer has the Z motor plugged into a different connector on the board (the one on the right). Is this a problem? What's the difference?

replies.content: Hi. The Z motors move simultaneously, so it doesn't really make any difference in which Z port they are plugged in.
